data.narrative:
Claros is a Seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Daniel Kultran and Grant Verstandig that has raised $30M to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector comprises 1 public comparable (Linzatech, ticker LNZA) and 8 private peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix. However, same-stage and adjacent-stage peer filtering within this universe yielded insufficient datapoints (fewer than 3) to support a reliable peer-median valuation, necessitating reliance on stage-progression methodology.

Stage-progression analysis applies a 2.5x multiplier to the $30M total raised, treating total capital raised as a valuation proxy and applying typical Seed-to-next-stage step-ups observed in frontier technology. This method yields an implied valuation of $75M. Sensitivity around this figure—accounting for execution risk and the early-stage nature of the company—produces a triangulated range of $64M (low) to $86M (high), with $75M as the median point.

The valuation rests primarily on a single methodology given peer-set constraints. Key uncertainties include technology de-risking trajectory, capital efficiency relative to sector benchmarks, and whether the Seed-to-Series A step-up multiplier of 2.5x accurately reflects frontier-tech risk profiles. The analysis would benefit from additional market data as comparable exit multiples and later-stage fundraises within Climate & Energy mature.
